moment: The person looks for a key on the computer.
does: Lists, in one short paragraph, the keys that work on this page when a keyboard is attached. The Space bar and also the arrow pointing down go one slide forward; the arrow pointing up goes one slide back; the slash key opens the search; C jumps to the chorus, V to the verse after this one, B to the bridge; a digit from 1 to 9 jumps to that part of the song; F1 hides the words, F2 makes the screen black, F3 shows the logo, F6 switches the projector on or off.
register: The page speaks to a volunteer holding a phone at the console or standing beside the stage: any age, no time to read, thumb-sized buttons. Plain, short, polite and familiar. No honorifics, no jargon.
notes: Key names stay as printed on the keyboard. Every key in the list above must be named, and no other. It is a paragraph that wraps over several lines on the phone, so write whole short sentences; no slashes standing in for words.

screen: The phone remote: a web page opened on the volunteer's own phone (about 360 points wide, one hand, often in the dark), joined to the operator computer over the church's wireless network. Dark screens with no row of tabs. Live screen: a top bar with a two-segment switch (Live, Plan) and two round buttons (search, a gear); under it the title of what is open with a slide counter, the live slide at full width, Back and Next as two large buttons side by side, four state buttons in one grouped row, and at the bottom a drawer with the song's sections as buttons and the slides as labelled thumbnails. The same yellow pill at the top right of the slide, where the page also says that the screen is black or that the words are hidden.
moment: The Live switch is off: the slide in the card is in place and the room does not see it.
does: Says the projector is switched off, so the person knows why the room sees nothing.
register: The page speaks to a church volunteer holding a phone: any age, in the middle of a service, with no time to read. Plain, short, polite and familiar. No honorific for the reader, no jargon, no slang.
notes: A short statement without a full stop, with the same word for off that the operator's window uses for the projector.
